notes:
Attendance settings can now forgive one morning at a time. The grace window under Late marking still sets the everyday rule, and a new list beneath it names the days that were not everyday — a downpour, a transport strike, the morning after a company function. A date in that list uses its own window instead, for everyone, on that day alone: the workday still starts at its usual time, so a late arrival is still measured from there. Each row says when late starts on that day, why it was different, and who set it. Super Admin only, like the rest of the late-marking rules.

Leave now reaches the CEO and the MD. They see every leave request in their company — including the ones sitting with somebody else — and are told as soon as one is filed. They can settle any of them out of turn: the buttons say Override, a reason is required, the approvers who were skipped are told it went over their heads, and the decision is recorded against the name of whoever made it.

A leave that is already decided can be corrected too — its type, its dates, or what the day actually was — from My Approvals and from Admin → Leave, which now offers the same correction sheet. Changing what a day was puts those days back on the attendance calendar, or takes them off it, and the employee is told with the reason.

Every leave request now carries its own trail: who has changed it since it was filed, and which of those changes were somebody overruling the approvers. It reads on the leave queue, in History and on the admin leave list, so HR and the Super Admin can see at a glance what was altered and by whom.

For everybody else nothing changes.
